Run the three “Next Commands” in order from the repo root (same environment you used for previous baselines). They cover: (1) module-level AUB tuning and best selection, (2) system-level candidate runs, (3) generating a prioritized fix list based on latest results.

```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best

python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run

python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

### What to expect / what to check after each
1) **`aub_autopilot.py --run --select-best`**
- Runs AUB evaluations across modules in `module_registry.yaml`.
- Chooses the best-performing candidate(s) and updates the registry/baseline artifacts (depending on your tool’s behavior).
- After it finishes, check:
  - Any updated “best” pointers (often in a registry JSON/YAML or “latest” files).
  - The report/logs for whether the champion changed from `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`.

2) **`system_autopilot.py --run`**
- Executes end-to-end system candidates from `system_candidates.yaml`.
- Produces system-level metrics and any “PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE” classification your harness uses.
- After it finishes, check:
  - The generated run summaries (typically under `baseline/reports/` or an `outputs/` directory).
  - Whether any candidate becomes a new PASS candidate (your handoff currently shows none).

3) **`aub_next_fix.py`**
- Generates `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` with recommended next actions (usually the highest-impact module regressions or weak spots).
- This is the quickest way to decide what to change next if the autopilots don’t yield a clear winner.

### If anything fails
Paste the last ~80 lines of the failing command output plus:
- the directory listing of the output/report folder it mentions, and
- the current contents (or diff) of any file it claims to update (registry/champion pointer),
and I can tell you exactly what to fix and what to rerun.
